narrative.overview: The site is a datasheet for an engineer, page 1 first. It borrows the reader's own document: a part number in the strip, a pinout as the hero, numbered sections, ruled tables, figure and table captions, status stamps, and errata. Every value on the page is a measured, sourced number. Decoration comes only from the datasheet's own vocabulary and the circuit board it describes.
keyCharacteristics: Pinout hero that doubles as navigation (link pins are real anchors).
Numbered datasheet sections, each opened by a copper trace rule.
Ruled tables (2px top and bottom, hairline rows) for all structured content.
Mono for data, units, labels, captions; condensed Archivo for display, normal-width Archivo for reading.
Status stamps (PRELIMINARY, ADVANCE INFORMATION) used only where the status is true.

rules.name: The Two Traces Rule
rules.body: Copper and signal blue are the only accents. Copper means "this is the work"; blue means "you can go here". Never swap them, never add a third.

rules.name: The PCB Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is soldermask green-black, never neutral gray or pure black; text is silkscreen off-white.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is for values, units, identifiers, pins, and captions. Never for prose or headings.

dos: Do source every number from content/ and label simulated or schematic material as such.
Do use the datasheet's own devices (sections, tables, captions, stamps, errata) instead of cards.
Do keep copper for the work and blue for links.
Do keep motion to traces drawing in, and render them fully drawn under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, drop shadows, or card grids.
Don't add proficiency bars, ratings, or invented specs.
Don't put eyebrow labels above headings; the section number sits inline in the heading.
